Datacenter Power & Cooling Systems Overview
Reference document describing the power distribution and cooling infrastructure across the facility's
server halls.
1. Power Distribution
Utility power enters the facility through two independent feeds from separate substations, providing N+1
redundancy at the facility level. Each feed is rated for 2.5 MW. Power passes through automatic
transfer switches (ATS) before reaching the uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems, which provide
ride-through power during the transfer window and during the startup of backup generators. Three
diesel generators, each rated at 1.2 MW, provide backup power and can sustain full facility load with
one generator offline for maintenance (N+1 generator redundancy).
2. UPS Configuration
UPS units are configured in a 2N topology per server hall, meaning each hall has two fully independent
UPS paths, either of which can carry the full hall load alone. Battery runtime at full load is rated at 12
minutes, sufficient to bridge the approximately 45-second generator startup and transfer window with
significant margin.
3. Cooling Systems
Cooling is provided by a chilled water system feeding in-row cooling units positioned between server
racks. Chilled water is produced by three chillers operating in an N+1 configuration, each rated at 400
tons of cooling capacity. Server halls are arranged in a hot-aisle/cold-aisle containment layout, which
improves cooling efficiency by preventing hot and cold air from mixing. Supply air temperature is
maintained at 22°C (72°F) with a target humidity range of 40-60% relative humidity.
4. Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE)
PUE is calculated as Total Facility Power divided by IT Equipment Power. The facility's measured PUE
over the past 12 months averaged 1.35, meaning for every 1 kW consumed by IT equipment, an
additional 0.35 kW is consumed by cooling, power distribution losses, and other overhead. The facility's
target PUE, set as part of the annual efficiency goal, is 1.25.

6. Maintenance Schedule

rows: In-row chilled water + rear-door heat exchangers

pages.text:
Generators are load-tested monthly for 30 minutes under simulated facility load. UPS battery health is
checked quarterly, with full battery replacement typically required every 5 years. Chiller maintenance
follows the manufacturer's schedule of semi-annual service, with the next scheduled service for all
three chillers falling in the third week of next month. Hall D's cooling system, being newly
commissioned, follows a more frequent monthly inspection schedule for its first year of operation.
